_comment: Guided tour of the native intensity-trace tool. Targets are the app's item_rects / spec action names; awaited steps wait for the user's own press.

steps.title: A trace is photons counted per time window
steps.text: Each detector's photons are counted in bins of the time window; the histogram beside each trace says how often each count occurs. Single molecules switching between states show up as jumps between levels.

steps.title: Start with data whose answer you know
steps.text: Example loads a simulated molecule that switches between two FRET states (visits of 20 and 80 ms) on two detectors. Two levels must be visible, anti-correlated between the detectors.

steps.title: The time window decides what you can resolve
steps.text: Short bins resolve fast switching but carry few photons each; long bins average short visits away. The file is binned again when you change it.

steps.title: Fit the hidden states
steps.text: Open the HMM tab, then Compute HMM: the model assigns every bin to a state (dimmest first) and writes burst IDs, traces and histograms beside the file.

steps.title: Compute HMM
steps.text: Two components for the example. The states and the FRET trace appear under the traces.

steps.title: How long each state lasts
steps.text: Dwell Times: one histogram per state with an exponential fit. A visit shorter than a few bins is not resolved, so the fitted times come out somewhat longer than the simulated 20 / 80 ms.

steps.title: How many states?
steps.text: BIC Elbow fits 1 to 15 states; where the curve stops falling is the number the data support.
